description:
A conflict resolution can silently delete work that has already merged, and nothing in the merge floor notices. The floor rebases onto the latest base and re-verifies, which catches TEXTUAL interference (a conflict) and STALENESS (a red gate). It never compares what a rebase REMOVED against what landed on the base while the branch was in flight, so a resolution that throws the base side away passes both.

THE INCIDENT, in a downstream repository. A tasklist branch reached the merge floor about eight days stale. Its rebase onto the base conflicted, and the agent resolving it was working from chief's instruction to rebase and resolve 'keeping BOTH sides' intent'. The replayed commit nonetheless kept the BRANCH's stale copy of two whole files. That erased what seven already-merged tasklists had added to them: a module declaration, about two dozen command registrations, a validation check, a UI warning, and several tests. The agent then fixed only what the compiler flagged, the verify gate went green, and chief merged. Every layer that could have noticed was blind to this shape by construction. A deleted test cannot fail. An undeclared module is not compiled, so its errors vanish with it. Commands registered by string name are checked by no compiler. The gate was green because the evidence had been deleted along with the work.

WHERE THE RESOLUTION HAPPENS. The merge floor itself never resolves a conflict: a REBASE-CONFLICT stops the tasklist, and ROADMAP's 'No AI auto-conflict-resolution' row stays true. Chief hands resolution off in two places.
  (1) integrate_base's conflict arm (engine/driver.sh), at pickup or at an iteration boundary. It ABORTS its own rebase and writes .chief/state/INTEGRATE-BASE.md, which tells the agent to `git rebase <base>` and, at each stop, 'resolve the conflicts keeping BOTH sides' intent — the <base> side is already-merged work, so never discard it, and never discard your own'.
  (2) conflict_report's 'Resolve it' runbook, written on a REBASE-CONFLICT stop in the serialized floor and in the merge queue's mq_stack_member. It tells a human, or the next run's agent, to do the same by hand.
Either way the resolved branch comes back to the floor ALREADY rebased. It takes the 'strictly ahead of <base> — rebase is a no-op' arm, verifies green and merges. The floor's own rebase never sees the conflict it exists to catch.

WHAT CHIEF RECORDS TODAY, AND WHAT IT THROWS AWAY. No durable record holds a branch's original fork point or its pre-rebase tip.
  - The worktree is created with `git worktree add -b <branch> <base>`, and the base sha is written nowhere.
  - integrate_base writes the base tip it integrated against to $wt/.chief/state/.integrated-base. That file is inside the worktree, which run_worker deletes at the top of every run. It is a THROTTLE key, not a fork record: it is written before acting, on clean and conflicted attempts alike.
  - The merge phase reads `pre_mb` (the merge-base of branch and base) just before its rebase. For a branch the agent already rebased, that is the NEW base, not the original fork, and it feeds conflict_report only.
  - The branch reflog would hold the pre-rebase tip, but chief does not control it: reflogs can be disabled or expire, and they go when the branch is deleted, which chief does on merge.
So the check needs a record chief writes itself, under the driver's durable state and never under the worktree (CLAUDE.md's durable-state invariant).

THE PRECISE CHECK. The branch's intended change is its PRE-rebase diff (original fork to original tip). After the rebase, the post-rebase diff runs from the new fork to the new tip. A line qualifies as deleted by the resolution when all three hold: the post-rebase diff removes it, the pre-rebase diff did NOT remove it, and it is present in the new base. Attribute each such line to the base commit that introduced it (between the original fork and the new base). When that commit arrived through a chief auto-merge ('Merge chief/<stem> (chief, auto-verified)'), also name the sibling tasklist, the way conflict_report already does for conflicted files.
Two edges the definition must settle rather than ignore:
  - A base line the resolution only MOVED within its file is still present at the tip, so it is not a loss.
  - A commit made AFTER the resolution (a later story legitimately removing a line the base added) also appears in the post-minus-pre difference. Either the check excludes it precisely (the replayed commits are the ones with a pre-rebase counterpart; commits authored after the integration have none), or it flags it and the override covers it. Choose, justify the choice with a measurement in notes, and pin it in a test. A mistake in the permissive direction repeats the incident; a mistake in the strict direction costs one `chief approve`.

ENFORCEMENT REUSES THE POLICY LAYER; IT DOES NOT INVENT ONE. zones_merge_gate (engine/zones.sh) is already the merge phase's one 'green is not enough authority' question. budget_holds (engine/budget.sh) shows how a second rule joins it: it contributes zone-shaped hold lines, and the branch is held AWAITING-APPROVAL with one request file, one checksum-bound verdict and one `chief approve`. A resolution-deletion finding joins the same way, with one difference. A review zone and a budget in `block` mode are opt-in; this rule is not, and it must stay armed when a repo has no zones.conf or has disarmed its review rules. Both merge paths already call zones_merge_gate (driver.sh and mergequeue.sh), so folding the rule in there covers the batch queue too. One gap in the house pattern must be closed rather than inherited: zones_clear_record deletes the approval file on merge, so an override that must stay RECORDED has to land somewhere that outlives the merge.

Keep the detector out of the driver's worker body. The quality ratchet's function_length_max counts raw line span, and the merge phase already sits inside a very long function. The detector belongs in its own engine module, sourced the way budget.sh and zones.sh are, with a line in CLAUDE.md's layout.

NOT IN SCOPE. The merge-policy approval-flow rework (ROADMAP's Planned row). This tasklist adds a hold whose finding is line-precise, which is the kind of hold that earns its friction, but it does not change how holds are presented or approved. Chief still does not resolve conflicts itself.

FIELD CALIBRATION — a read-only sweep of ~1,300 chief merges across 28 repositories (2026-09-11) found the incident above to be the ONLY confirmed casualty; 100 other flagged merges were benign. The shapes a detector must NOT trip on: (1) in-place forward edits — a line the merging branch extended or reworded shows as removed; pair each removed line with similar added lines in the same file (ratio >= 0.6) and call it a revert only when the replacement text already existed in the file BEFORE the other tasklist landed — the incident restored 143 such pre-existing lines, every benign merge 0-8, the sharpest single signal; (2) counters and versions every merge bumps (VERSION, schema and IR versions, counts in prose) — the value only moves forward; (3) regenerated files (hash pins, inventories, reports, generated export trees); (4) intentional retire/supersede — only the merging tasklist's own record tells it apart; (5) blame credits the LAST tasklist whose merge touched a line, not its author — accept any tasklist that landed after the branch's first commit, or attribute with `blame -C`; (6) symbol inventories are a cheap, strong cross-check — registered commands, test counts, module declarations before vs after (the incident went 68 -> 44 registered commands). US-1's pre-rebase vs post-rebase diff comparison sidesteps most of these because it compares the branch against its own intent rather than against history; any fallback heuristic must respect them. Also: the in-flight test depends on rebase preserving author dates — if chief ever resets them, it breaks.

userStories.title: Chief can say which lines a resolution deleted, and whose work they were
acceptanceCriteria: The branch's ORIGINAL fork point and its PRE-rebase tip are recorded durably, under the driver's state directory and never the worktree (which run_worker deletes every run). They are recorded at every point where chief hands a conflict to someone else to resolve: integrate_base's conflict arm, and the REBASE-CONFLICT arm of both the serialized merge floor and the merge queue. The fork point is also recorded at branch creation if the check needs it. The record survives a run ending and a later run resuming the branch, and it is cleared when the tasklist merges, along with the other per-tasklist artifacts that are cleared there.

A detector takes the recorded (fork, pre-rebase tip) and the branch's current (base, tip). It prints every line that the post-rebase diff removes, that the pre-rebase diff did not remove, that is present in the new base, and that no longer appears in that file at the tip. Each line is printed with its file, its text, and the base commit that introduced it; when that commit arrived through a chief auto-merge, the sibling tasklist's name is printed too.

The post-resolution-commit edge is settled. A line removed by a commit made after the resolution (one with no pre-rebase counterpart) is either excluded precisely or flagged by design. Notes record which was chosen, why, and the measurement behind it, and a test pins the choice. Binary and renamed paths are either checked or reported as UNCHECKED; they are never silently skipped.

Unit tests source the module directly (no driver) and run it against temp repos. The incident shape (the base adds a line after the fork; the resolution keeps the branch's stale copy of the whole file) is FLAGGED with that line, its file and its commit. A line the branch's own pre-rebase diff removes is NOT flagged. A clean rebase yields nothing. A base line the resolution only moved within the file is NOT flagged.
The detector lives in its own engine module, sourced by the driver rather than added to the worker body, and CLAUDE.md's layout has a line for it.
GATES: `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; `test/{smoke,ratelimit,noworkguard}.sh` green; `VERSION` bumped (`test/version-bump.sh`); `ROADMAP.md` names this stem (`test/doc-sync.sh`).
userStories.notes: test/resolution-deletions.sh: 30/30 assertions passed (the incident FLAGGED with its line, file and sibling `77-register-commands`; branch-intent, a clean rebase, a moved base line, a re-added line and a later commit all NOT flagged). shellcheck -S error over bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh + install.sh: exit 0; bash -n clean. smoke PASS (12.9s), ratelimit rc=0, noworkguard rc=0, version-bump rc=0 (VERSION 0.9.25 -> 0.9.26), doc-sync rc=0, quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 613 -> 618, tol 15 — the detector is its own module, not worker body). POST-RESOLUTION-COMMIT EDGE: EXCLUDED PRECISELY, not flagged. A rebase preserves author date, author and subject, so a post-rebase commit is a REPLAY when some pre-rebase commit shares that key; the measured window is newFork..<newest replayed commit>, and a commit authored after the integration has no counterpart and falls outside it. Chosen because resolving and then implementing the story in the same iteration is the COMMON path, so flagging it would fire on most conflicted branches. MEASURED (section E): same fixture, resolution correct, then a later commit legitimately removes the base's line — 0 findings with the window, and the same test asserts the UNWINDOWED diff (newFork..tip) DOES remove that line, so the window is provably what excluded it. A commit interleaved after a replay stays inside the window and can only over-report, which is the one-`chief approve` direction. Binary and renamed paths are emitted as UNCHECKED records, never skipped; an unreadable pre-rebase tip is UNCHECKED too. Removals are NET of re-adds — found while writing the test: a base file whose last line lacked a trailing newline has that line rewritten by any append, and the removal half alone flagged it.

userStories.title: A merge that would erase merged work is held, and the hold names whose work it was
acceptanceCriteria: When the detector reports at least one line, the merge does not happen. The branch is held through the existing policy layer: the finding joins zones_merge_gate as zone-shaped hold lines, the way budget_holds does, and the tasklist ends AWAITING-APPROVAL with its branch kept, rebased and green. There is no new park state and no new approval command.

The hold names each file, each deleted line, and each base commit and sibling tasklist whose work would be lost. It does so in the worker log, the approval request file, the run summary's awaiting-approval block and `chief approve --list`. A long list is truncated with a count, never silently.
The hold is always armed. It applies with no .chief/zones.conf, with every zone rule set to `serialize`, and under CHIEF_DIFF_BUDGET=warn and =off. A test shows each case.

The override is `chief approve <name> -m <reason>`. The approval is bound by checksum to exactly the flagged lines, so a re-resolution that deletes something different asks again. The approval, with who, when, the note and the lines it covered, survives the merge in the tasklist's completed/ record. zones_clear_record deletes the approval file on merge, so the file alone is not a record.
Both merge paths are covered: the serialized floor and the opt-in merge queue, which both call zones_merge_gate. Notes say how the batch path was checked.

The cost is measured and the run condition is decided. Either the check runs only when US-1 recorded a resolution for this branch, or it runs on every merge because the measured cost is negligible. Notes record the measurement (wall time and git invocations on a realistic branch) and the choice. If the conditional path is chosen, a branch with no recorded resolution pays at most one file-existence test.

test/stale-resume.sh, test/conflict-forensics.sh, test/overlap-zones.sh and test/merge-batch.sh stay green. If an existing fixture's scripted resolution itself drops base lines, that fixture was modelling the bug: fix the fixture, never loosen the rule, and say so in notes.

The rule is documented where the policy layer is documented (docs/reference/overlap-zones.md, or a new reference doc with the Status · Updated · Owner banner, linked from docs/README.md). The doc states the rule's limit: it sees deleted lines, not broken meaning. A resolution that keeps every base line but changes what they do is still the verify gate's business.
GATES: `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; `test/{smoke,ratelimit,noworkguard}.sh` green; `VERSION` bumped (`test/version-bump.sh`); `ROADMAP.md` names this stem (`test/doc-sync.sh`).
userStories.notes: test/resolution-deletions.sh: 59/59 assertions passed (was 30 — sections J..O are this story), 8.2s, no driver. GATES: shellcheck -S error over bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh + install.sh exit 0; bash -n clean; smoke PASS, ratelimit rc=0, noworkguard rc=0, version-bump rc=0 (VERSION 0.9.26 -> 0.9.27, README+ROADMAP bold with it), doc-sync PASS (48 merged tasklists named), quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 613 -> 618, tol 15; single_use_functions 40 -> 40). REGRESSION SET all green and UNCHANGED — no fixture had to be loosened: overlap-zones PASS (A-E), stale-resume PASS, conflict-forensics PASS, merge-batch PASS (A-F). HOW IT HOLDS: resolution_holds emits the finding as zone-shaped `review resolution:deleted` lines and zones_merge_gate composes them beside budget_holds, so the hold reuses the one request file, one checksum and one `chief approve` — no new park state, no new command. ALWAYS ARMED, asserted four ways in section J: no .chief/zones.conf at all, a registry of only `serialize` rules, CHIEF_DIFF_BUDGET=warn, CHIEF_DIFF_BUDGET=off — held in all four. NAMED IN ALL FOUR PLACES (section K): worker log ('would ERASE 1 line(s)' + file + line + sibling 77-register-commands), the request JSON, the run summary's awaiting-approval block and `chief approve --list` (the last two are asserted through the exact renders driver.sh and zones_show use, not assumed from the file). Truncation is `… and N more erased line(s) (M in total)`. BINDING (section L): the hold's FIRST line is a summary carrying a cksum id over the WHOLE finding, so truncation cannot loosen the binding. Measured: same file, same story, same changed-file set — erasing DELTA_TWO gave change id 4070398514-342, re-resolving to erase DELTA_ONE too gave 3207872277-492, and the banked approval no longer matched (held again). zones_stamp_record folds the verdict into completed/<name>.json as .approval (by, at, note, zones = the erased lines) inside finalize_merged, which runs BEFORE zones_clear_record at both merge sites; asserted to survive the clear. BATCH PATH (section O, criterion 5): both paths call zones_merge_gate, and the batch differs only in SCOPE, so the rule is measured from $scope (the tip the member was stacked on) and not $base. Checked with a fixture where a PEER legitimately removes a base line: stacked on the peer the member is NOT held; measured from the base it IS — so the negative half fails on the wrong plumbing rather than passing by coincidence. test/merge-batch.sh PART C (a held member in a batch) still passes untouched. COST, and the run condition (criterion 6): RUNS ON EVERY MERGE. No recorded resolution = ZERO git invocations (asserted under a counting git shim in section N) and ~0.8 ms per call over 100 calls. A recorded one, measured on this real branch (12 files, 683 changed lines): 1.05 s wall and 61 git invocations — against a merge phase that has just paid the full verify gate (~10 min). A conditional path would have bought ~1 s and added a place the check can fail to run. DOC: new docs/reference/resolution-deletions.md (Status/Updated/Owner banner), linked from docs/README.md and cross-linked from overlap-zones.md's now-three-rules section; it states the limit — it sees deleted LINES, not broken meaning, and a resolution that keeps every base line and changes what they do is still the verify gate's business. check-doc-links: 0 dead references.

userStories.title: The resolution instruction shows what the base changed, and requires keeping it
acceptanceCriteria: The INTEGRATE-BASE note that integrate_base writes no longer stops at 'keeping BOTH sides' intent'. For each conflicted file, it includes what the base changed in that file since the fork point: the `git diff <fork>..<base> -- <file>` hunks, bounded, with an over-limit diff truncated to its size plus the exact command that shows all of it. It states that those changes are already-merged work that must still be present after the resolution, and that chief compares the result and holds the merge if they are not.

The note names the trap by its mechanism. Taking one side of a whole file during a rebase discards every base-side change in that file, conflicted hunks or not. It also says that in a rebase `--ours` is the base and `--theirs` is the branch's commit being replayed, the reverse of a merge.

conflict_report's 'Resolve it' runbook, for REBASE-CONFLICT and MERGE-CONFLICT, carries the same per-file base-side diff and the same requirement, because a human or the next run's agent resolves from it.

A test asserts that the note handed to the agent carries the base-side diff. The fixture plants a unique marker line on the base after the fork, and the note contains that marker under the conflicted file's entry. The assertion is on the planted marker plus a string only the engine emits, never on a heading that templates/agent-context.md quotes.
GATES: `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; `test/{smoke,ratelimit,noworkguard}.sh` green; `VERSION` bumped (`test/version-bump.sh`); `ROADMAP.md` names this stem (`test/doc-sync.sh`).
userStories.notes: test/stale-resume.sh PASS (49s) and test/conflict-forensics.sh PASS (33s) — both extended, both MUTATION-CHECKED. GATES: shellcheck -S error over bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh + install.sh exit 0; bash -n clean over the same set; smoke PASS, ratelimit rc=0, noworkguard rc=0; version-bump PASS (VERSION 0.9.27 -> 0.9.28, README + ROADMAP bold with it); doc-sync PASS (48 merged tasklists named); resolution-deletions 59/59 (unchanged); quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 613 -> 618 tol 15, single_use_functions 53 -> 53 tol 2 — both new helpers have two call sites); check-doc-links 0 dead references. WHAT THE NOTE NOW CARRIES: `resolution_keep_base_requirement` + `resolution_base_side_diff` (engine/resolution.sh, the instruction half beside the check half) emit, per conflicted file, `git diff <fork>..<base> -- <file>` under a `### <file>` heading, bounded at CHIEF_RESOLUTION_DIFF_LINES (default 80) lines and CHIEF_RESOLUTION_DIFF_FILES (default 12) files — an over-limit diff is cut and followed by its REAL size plus the exact `git -C <repo> diff <fork>..<base> -- <file>` that shows the rest, and extra files are named with a count, never dropped silently. A file the base never touched prints "nothing on `<base>` changed this file since the fork" rather than nothing. The prose states the hunks are already-merged work that must STILL BE PRESENT afterwards and that chief compares and HOLDS the merge (AWAITING-APPROVAL); it names the trap by its MECHANISM (taking one side of a whole file discards every base-side change in that file, not only the conflicted hunks — the non-conflicting ones being exactly those never on screen); and it states that in a REBASE `--ours` is the base and `--theirs` is the commit being replayed, the reverse of a merge. BOTH HANDOFFS carry the identical text from the same two functions: integrate_base's INTEGRATE-BASE.md (fork = merge-base(branch, base), scoped to the unmerged paths of the stopped rebase) and conflict_report's runbook, which serves REBASE-CONFLICT and MERGE-CONFLICT alike and measures from the `mb` it is already handed; its step-2/runbook prose now points AT the section. TEST EVIDENCE: stale-resume ARM B plants a unique non-conflicting base line (SR-B-BASE-MARKER-7c31) beside the conflicting one and asserts it appears as an ADDED line (`+SR-B-BASE-MARKER-7c31`) under `### shared.txt`, in the note on disk AND in the evidence copy the agent was actually handed; conflict-forensics plants CF-BASE-MARKER-3ab7 the same way and asserts it under the report's own base-side section. Every assertion is on the planted marker plus a string only the engine emits ("discards **every** base-side change in", "**In a rebase the sides are reversed from a merge:**", "HOLDS the merge (AWAITING-APPROVAL)") — none of them is a heading templates/agent-context.md quotes (grepped: templates/agent-context.md, engine/instructions.md and engine/plan-instructions.md contain none of these strings). MUTATION MEASURED: with the two calls removed from integrate_base and everything else identical, test/stale-resume.sh exits 1 with "B: the note does not show what the base changed under the conflicted file (marker SR-B-BASE-MARKER-7c31 absent)" — so the assertion fails on the engine, not on the fixture.

userStories.title: The incident is reproduced end to end, and so are the merges that must still happen
acceptanceCriteria: A new hermetic test drives the real driver with a scripted fake agent in a temp repo. The base gains a line in a shared file after the branch forks. The branch's own edit to that file conflicts. The agent resolves as in the incident, by keeping the branch's stale copy of the whole file, and verify comes back green. Asserted: the tasklist is NOT merged, the base did not move, the status is AWAITING-APPROVAL, and the report names the file, the planted line and the base commit that added it.

The test is mutation-checked. With the detector neutered in a copy of the engine (not `git show HEAD~N`, because CI clones shallow), the same fixture MERGES. Notes record that observed run, so the test is shown to reproduce the incident rather than restate behaviour that always worked.
Negative control (a): a branch whose pre-rebase diff intentionally deletes a line conflicts, is resolved correctly, and merges with no hold.
Negative control (b): a branch that rebases cleanly (the base advanced on an unrelated file, so no resolution was needed) merges unchanged. Notes record what the check cost on that path.
Override: running `chief approve <name> -m <reason>` on the held tasklist and then `chief run` merges it, and the completed record carries the approval with its note and the lines it covered.

The new test file is in all three gate lists: .chief/verify.sh's CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS, test/all.sh's BASH_SUITE, and .github/workflows/ci.yml. ci.yml still parses (`python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"`).
GATES: `bash -n` + `shellcheck -S error` clean; `test/{smoke,ratelimit,noworkguard}.sh` green; `VERSION` bumped (`test/version-bump.sh`); `ROADMAP.md` names this stem (`test/doc-sync.sh`).
userStories.notes: test/resolution-incident.sh: PASS, 36s, 5 parts (A incident held · B mutation · C negative control (a) · D negative control (b) · E override) — the real driver, a real worktree, a real pickup conflict, a real merge phase; nothing in it calls an engine function by name. GATES: bash -n clean over bin/chief + engine/*.sh + test/*.sh + install.sh + scripts/*.sh; shellcheck -S error over the same set exit 0; smoke PASS, ratelimit rc=0, noworkguard rc=0; version-bump rc=0 (VERSION 0.9.28 -> 0.9.29, README + ROADMAP bold with it); doc-sync PASS (48 merged tasklists named); quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 613 -> 618 tol 15, single_use_functions 56 -> 56 tol 2, duplicate_blocks 19 -> 19); check-doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main; ci.yml re-parsed with yaml.safe_load (1 job, `test`). THREE GATE LISTS, all three edited: .chief/verify.sh's CHIEF_BYSTANDER_TESTS, test/all.sh's BASH_SUITE, .github/workflows/ci.yml. PART A (the incident): a branch forks, a sibling merge lands on the base editing shared.txt with ONE line that collides and TWO that do not (RI-BASE-MARKER-4f2a and "a sibling registered another command" — the incident's shape: base-side work in the same FILE but not in the conflicted HUNK). The pickup rebase conflicts, chief hands it off, and the scripted agent does what the incident's agent did — `git checkout --theirs -- <file>` during the rebase, which is the BRANCH's copy of the whole file, the mechanism and not a simulation of its outcome. verify came back "verify: ok" and the tasklist still ended AWAITING-APPROVAL: main at exactly the sha it started at, out/inc/US-2.txt not on main, no completed/ record, branch kept. The report names shared.txt, BOTH erased lines, the base commit's short sha and the sibling tasklist 61-register-commands — asserted in the worker log, in the .zone-request.json, in the run summary's AWAITING APPROVAL block and in `chief approve --list`. PART B, THE MUTATION RUN, OBSERVED: the tool root is copied to $WORK/unfixed and resolution_deletions() is rewritten to `return 0` (awk, anchored on the function header, with an explicit failure if the anchor ever moves and a bash -n on the result — a copy and not `git show HEAD~N`, because CI clones shallow). The SAME fixture, built by the same function with the same scripted agent, then runs against that copy and reports MERGED @<sha>, main MOVES, and `git show main:shared.txt` no longer contains RI-BASE-MARKER-4f2a or the sibling's second line — the incident, on the base branch, under a green gate. So PART A fails on the detector rather than on behaviour that always worked. NEGATIVE CONTROL (a) — PART C: a branch whose own pre-rebase diff DELETES a line (DOOMED-LINE) while the base adds RI-NEGA-BASE-MARKER-9d17 right beside it; the rebase conflicts (asserted: "does NOT rebase cleanly" plus a marker the fake agent drops only when it actually resolved, so the arm cannot pass by never conflicting) and the resolution honours both sides. MERGED, no "would ERASE", no "HELD BY THE MERGE POLICY LAYER", no .zone-request.json written at all; on main the base marker is present and DOOMED-LINE is gone. NEGATIVE CONTROL (b) — PART D: the base advances on an unrelated file, the pickup rebase is clean ("rebased chief/negb onto main"), no conflict is ever handed off, and the tasklist merges unchanged. COST ON THAT PATH, MEASURED: no handoff means no record, so resolution_deletions takes its fast path — 0 git invocations (counted under a PATH `git` shim over 100 calls) and 1.9 ms per call, i.e. one file-existence test. Pinned in the test rather than left in prose: neither $STATE/negb.resolution.json nor refs/chief/resolution/negb is ever created, so there is nothing to clear at merge either. OVERRIDE — PART E: `chief approve inc -m "<reason>"` then a second `chief run inc` merges (status MERGED, state done, out/inc/US-2.txt on main) and spends NO further agent turn (call count unchanged). completed/inc.json carries .approval with decision=approved, the operator's note verbatim, by, at, and the zones it covered — including the resolution:deleted entry naming RI-BASE-MARKER-4f2a — while the .zone-request.json, .zone-approval.json, .resolution.json and the pin ref are all gone, which is exactly why the assertion had to be about the completed record.
